submission.natural_language_explanation: The negative pole fires where a clause is framed as someone's report, claim, guess or open question rather than as an asserted fact: it peaks on the complementizer ' that' after reportative or epistemic predicates ('reports that', 'claimed that', 'alleged that', 'suspects that', 'seems that', 'it is likely that'), on 'whether'/'if' introducing an embedded question, and on first-person hedges and direct questions ('I think', 'I guess', 'I'm assuming', 'at a guess', 'Do I...?', 'Is that...?'). The same connectives inside a factive or certain frame ('confirmed that', 'knew that', 'the fact that', 'it is clear that'), with a demonstrative 'that', and in plain declarative prose stay near baseline, while the opposite pole is the explanation direction: its output promotes cause and source words ('the reason', 'cause', 'culprit', 'origin', 'blame') and it fires on explicit explanation ('the reasons can be explained by', 'possible mechanisms for', 'what could account for').

Pod spec lint fail validation: no known class method for selector

I'm trying to create a pod, my framework is building fine and I have no problem using it projects, but when I am trying to convert it into a pod and run pod spec lint to validate it it fails, and gives me the following error:
 - ERROR | [iOS] xcodebuild:  SimpleCameraFramework/SimpleCameraFramework/AVCaptureSession+Safe.m:28:67: error: no known class method for selector 'safeCastFromObject:'

In this file I have no compiler error, I have exposed the category in the umbrella header, so I really don't see where the problem is... Any idea?

A:

I found out the problem, for some reason the pod doesn't work with the precompiled header, if I remove it and import the .h file directly in AVCaptureSession+Safe, it works...

For example, a 1995 study by the Harvard School of Public Health indicated that people will forgo a stronger income scenario in favour of a weaker one as long as it meant earning more than their neighbours.

Unfortunately, many in the investment world are keenly aware of this and will structure their marketing efforts accordingly. As a result, you have a compounding of momentum or trends in the market as investors buy at or near market tops for fear of not doing as well as or better than others.

Only a couple of weeks into the current wave of violence, now widely referred to as the "third intifada," came the first attack by a woman: On September 22 Hadeel al-Hashlamon, a 19 year old, attempted to stab an Israeli soldier at a checkpoint in the West Bank.

Stereotypically, women have traditionally been seen as the victims of violence, whether domestic or political. However, the historical record makes it clear that women have not just been the passive victims of terrorism, but also have played an active role. In Muslim history, although women took part in battles at the time of the Prophet Mohammed, their participation was gradually restricted, as women's roles became consigned to the private sphere. Due to their proportionally greater prominence, Palestinian women have historically been seen by academics and the media as among some of the most liberated women in Arab society.

Women make good terrorists. They offer a strategic advantage in conducting terrorist attacks; as women do not conform to traditional security profiles, they typically arouse less suspicion, and their actions often garner more international media attention.

While the First Intifada saw both Palestinian men and women take part in violence against Israel, the Second Intifada was more male dominated. Women were excluded from many aspects of the public and political spheres of the movement. While women did participant and initiate attacks during the Second Intifada, it was rarer, and the violence was mostly carried out and dominated by men and male-controlled organizations.

While Palestinian organizations, especially religious organizations like Hamas and the Palestinian Islamic Jihad, were in the past reluctant to use women in terrorism, they began to change their tune in the early 2000's. Hamas' spiritual leader, Sheikh Ahmed Yassin (assassinated by Israel in 2004) went through a significant change in approach and rhetoric regarding the role women could play in attacks. In 2000 Sheikh Yassin stated that women's participation in martyrdom was problematic. However, by 2002, he noted that women, just like men, were drawn to jihad.

This current wave of terrorism has seen women playing a more prominent role in the violence rather than being relegated to secondary one. According to the IDF, since mid-September 2015, approximately 54 stabbing, shooting and vehicular attacks have occurred; of these attacks, women have been responsible for carrying out nine attacks, or approximately 16.6% of the terrorist attacks.

For example, on October 11, Israa Jaabis, 31, carried out a vehicular bombing in the West Bank; this was the first attack of its kind in this wave of terrorism. Other attacks by women include the October 7 stabbing in the Old City of Jerusalem, the October 12 stabbing at Ammunition Hill, the October 17 stabbing in Hebron, and the most recent October 25 attempted stabbing in Hebron.

Inorganic phosphate uptake in intact vacuoles isolated from suspension-cultured cells of Catharanthus roseus (L.) G. Don under varying Pi status.
Inorganic phosphate (Pi) uptake across the vacuolar membrane of intact vacuoles isolated from Catharanthus roseus suspension-cultured cells was measured. Under low Pi status, Pi uptake into the vacuole was strongly activated compared to high Pi status. Since Pi uptake across the vacuolar membrane is correlated with H+ pumping, we examined the dependency of H+ pumping on plant Pi status. Both H+ pumping and the activities of the vacuolar H+-pumps, the V-type H+-ATPase and the H+-PPase were enhanced under low Pi status. Despite this increase in H+ pumping, Western blot analysis showed no distinct increase in the amount of proton pump proteins. Possible mechanisms for the activation of Pi uptake into the vacuole under low Pi status are discussed.

Spain tops the ranking

According to the latest data from the European

The result of the average of the EU countries also
marks a clear dissimilarity with the Spanish context: six out of 10 Europeans live in a house opposite the remaining four does so in an apartment; more than 2.5 points of difference from the
Spanish proportion.

There are more home owners in Spain than in
other European countries.

Another interesting figure from Eurostat study on

(78.8%) own the property in which they live, 8.7% more than the European average. For rent they are somewhat below the average: 21.2% versus 29.9% for the European Community.

historical, economic and sociological.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Demonstrative 'that' used as a determiner, which the hypothesis explicitly predicts does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bicycle that he bought at the flea market last summer still leans against the garden wall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Relative-pronoun 'that' inside a noun phrase, not a complementizer introducing a reported, claimed or questioned clause.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The river rises after heavy rain, flows west through the valley, and joins the sea near the old lighthouse; fishermen know the current well.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Plain declarative prose with commas and a semicolon but no report, hedge or question, checking that delimiters alone do not drive the pole.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: If the pipe freezes overnight, the pump shuts down automatically and the alarm sounds in the control room.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Conditional 'if' introducing a condition rather than an embedded question, the near-miss for the claimed 'if' trigger.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I think about my grandmother whenever I pass the bakery on Fifth Street.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'I think' used as contemplation about a person rather than a first-person hedge, the same claimed words in another sense.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: This kind of oak grows best in sandy soil and tolerates long dry spells without extra watering.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'kind' as a noun classifier rather than the hedging 'kind of', the claimed token in another sense.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Bring a pen, a notebook, or a calculator to the exam and leave your phone in the locker.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'or' in a plain list of items rather than a hedge or an alternative question, testing the claimed token out of its claimed context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Do not touch the exposed wiring until the breaker has been switched off at the main panel.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'Do' as an imperative auxiliary rather than a question opener, the claimed token in the wrong construction.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The reasons for the outage can be explained by a failed cooling fan, and the likely culprit is a clogged intake filter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Explicit explanation with 'the reasons' and 'culprit', which the hypothesis assigns to the opposite pole, so this pole should stay near baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Local residents say the old mill has been sold to a developer, though no paperwork has been filed yet.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Reportative framing without the complementizer 'that' ('residents say'), a paraphrase holdout for the claimed report-not-assert feature.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Detectives suspect that the break-in was staged, and they allege that the owner filed a false insurance claim.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Two epistemic/reportative predicates with 'that' ('suspect that', 'allege that') in a novel police context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I'm assuming the replacement part ships tomorrow, since the supplier hasn't written back.
adversarial_test_results.detail: First-person hedge 'assuming' in a supply-chain context, a paraphrase of the claimed hedge feature.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We tested whether the coating survived the salt spray, and the results are still being analysed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'whether' introducing an embedded question in a lab-report genre unlike the top examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Do the new servers support the legacy storage protocol, or will we need an adapter for each drive?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Direct yes/no question opening with 'Do' and containing 'or', both claimed triggers, in a technical context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Incident review, Metro Line 3, control room logs. At 04:12 the supervisory control system reported a loss of telemetry from the eastern signalling block. The on-call engineer acknowledged the alarm, checked the redundant channel, and found it healthy. Traction power remained nominal throughout. The first trains of the morning departed from the depot on schedule, and the timetable recovered by 06:40 without manual intervention.

The maintenance crew inspected the block after the morning peak. Cabinet three showed no water ingress, the fibre terminations tested clean, and the backup battery held its charge. A firmware audit completed the previous quarter had found no deviations from the approved baseline, and the vendor's service bulletin for the unit had been applied in February. Spare parts for the block are held at the depot store, and the stock count at the end of the month matched the register.

Weather records for the night show light rain and a minimum temperature of four degrees, well inside the operating envelope for the equipment. The substation feeding the line logged no trips, and the uninterruptible supply at the control centre carried the load during the scheduled generator test at 03:30. The test finished early, and the generator was returned to standby before four o'clock.

Operations staff kept a written log of every radio call between 04:00 and 07:00. The log records routine exchanges between the driver of the first service and the signaller, a request to hold at platform two, and a short discussion about a door fault on the trailing carriage. None of these entries mention the eastern block, and the door fault cleared after the reset procedure. Training records show that all six signallers on the roster completed the refresher course in the spring, and two of them have since qualified as assessors.

The signalling block itself was returned to service at 09:15 after a supervised test. The test sequence exercised the telemetry path, the interlocking logic, and the trackside interface, and each stage completed without error. A repeat test at 11:00 gave the same result. The vendor's field engineer attended in the afternoon and downloaded the diagnostic archive from the block controller. The archive covers the seven days before the event, and it has been copied to the review folder for independent analysis.

The passenger information screens behaved as designed during the disruption. Announcements were made at each affected platform within two minutes of the first delay, and the accessibility line handled eleven calls. The review meeting was held on Thursday. One operator claims that the telemetry alarm had been suppressed during the overnight maintenance window, and a second engineer alleges that the suppression was left in place by mistake. The team has not established whether the suppression applied to the eastern block or only to the depot loops. Do the logs show any suppression command between 02:00 and 04:00, or was the alarm itself faulty? Until that question is answered, the review will remain open, and the recommendations will be limited to the door circuit and the battery replacement schedule.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long cross-genre operations memo with 'claims that', 'alleges that', 'whether' and a direct question buried deep in factual prose, testing the feature at distance in a genre absent from the examples.
